The bugs command

The bugs command files a bug report from the terminal and lists the reports you filed. This page lists each subcommand, its options and its exit codes.

Reference
  • Version 2.4
  • Updated 1 November 2026
  • Owner: Tools team

Install

Install the command with the package manager of your system. The command needs a sign-in token, which it asks for the first time you run it.

The token is kept in your home folder, in ~/.bugs/token. Delete the file to sign out.

Needs
  • Version 18 or later of Node.js
  • A sign-in token
# Install the command, then check the version
npm install --global @host/bugs
bugs --version

bugs new

Files a new bug report. With no options, the command asks for each field in turn. With options, it files the report at once and prints its number.

The command adds the version of the program and of your system to the report. Use --no-system to leave them out.

Returns
  • The number of the new report
  • Exit code 0 when it is filed
# File a report in one line, with a screenshot
bugs new --title "Export stops at 99 percent" --steps steps.txt --attach screen.png
# Filed report 4127. Follow it with: bugs show 4127
OptionValueWhat it doesDefault
--titleTextSets the title of the report. Keep it to one line that names what fails.Asked for
--stepsA file pathReads the steps to make the bug happen from a text file.Asked for
--attachA file pathAdds a file, such as a screenshot or a log. Use it more than once for more files.None
--no-systemNoneLeaves out the version of the program and of your system.Off
Warning

An attached log may hold private data, such as file paths or user names. Read the log before you attach it.

bugs list

Lists the reports you filed, newest first. Each line shows the number, the state and the title of a report.

Add --json to get the list as data for a script.

Returns
  • One line for each report
  • At most 50 lines
bugs list --state open
#  4127  open      Export stops at 99 percent
#  4093  open      Search ignores the date filter on the second page of results
#  3988  waiting   Crash when a file name holds an emoji
OptionValueWhat it doesDefault
--stateopen, waiting or closedShows only the reports in this state.All states
--limitA numberShows at most this many reports.50
--jsonNonePrints the list as JSON, one object for each report.Off

Exit codes

Every subcommand ends with one of these codes. A script can read the code to decide what to do next.

CodeMeaningWhat you doState
0The command worked.Nothing.Done
2An option is wrong or missing.Run the command with --help and fix the option.Fix, then run again
3The token is missing or has run out.Delete ~/.bugs/token and run the command again to sign in.Sign in, then run again
5The server did not answer.Wait a few minutes, then run the command again.Stop
